desc: Derive window cost formula: optimal target is a median; cost is sum of absolute deviations; for even x the lower median is valid and optimal.
Confirm "at least k" reduces to "exactly k" since all costs are nonnegative (dropping a window never increases total).
Implement coordinate compression plus two Fenwick trees (count and sum) for O(log n) sliding-window median and absolute-deviation cost over all length-x windows.
Implement the layered DP over window starts selecting k non-overlapping windows with transition dp[i][j] = min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i-x][j-1] + cost[i]) and handle indices/base cases.

Verify against both provided examples, edge cases (k=1, x=nums.length, minimum feasible placements, all-equal values), and a brute-force cross-check on small random inputs; reported PASS (samples 8 and 3, edge cases, and 3000 random brute-force cases).
